Microsoft Style Guide — summary (digest)
Plain language, consistency and clarity. Key rules:
- Write short sentences and paragraphs; one idea per sentence.
- Use active voice and strong verbs; say who does what.
- Cut unnecessary words (redundancy); avoid fluff.
- Use the present tense for instructions.
- Address the reader as 'you'; use imperative mood for instructions.
- Use one term consistently for a concept; avoid synonyms.
- Use standard punctuation; be consistent with serial commas.
- Avoid jargon, Latin phrases and idioms where a plain English
  alternative exists.
- Use numerals for numbers (10 and above; spell out below 10 except
  measurements, dates, money and percentages).
- Capitalization: sentence case for interface text and headlines
  unless a product name demands otherwise.
- Accessibility: descriptive link text, alternative text for images,
  no text on images, heading structure, sufficient contrast.
- Localization: keep strings short, avoid culture-bound references
  and images of text; follow the internationalization rules for dates,
  time, units.
